desc: Step-by-step Aircrack-ng reference: audit YOUR OWN WiFi — monitor mode, handshake capture, wordlist crack. Educational use only.
disclaimer: This documentation is provided strictly for educational and authorized purposes. Aircrack-ng captures wireless handshakes, so use it only on your own router and devices. Attacking anyone else's WiFi is illegal. The author and this site are not responsible for any misuse.
faq: Aircrack-ng is the classic WiFi auditing suite: put your adapter in monitor mode, capture the WPA handshake when your own device connects, then test it against a wordlist. It proves whether your WiFi passphrase survives a dictionary attack.
Auditing your own router is legal and recommended. Capturing handshakes or cracking passphrases for networks you do not own is illegal. Practice on your own router only.
What do I need for WiFi auditing?

A Linux machine (Kali ideal) plus a WiFi adapter that supports monitor mode and packet injection. Most laptop cards do monitor; cheap USB adapters (Atheros/Realtek chipsets) are the reliable lab choice.
Monitor mode tells the WiFi card to pass every nearby frame to Wireshark-style tools instead of only its own traffic. airmon-ng start wlan0 creates the mon0 interface auditors capture on.

When a device joins WPA2/WPA3, router and device exchange four cryptographic messages proving both know the passphrase — without sending it. Capturing those messages gives you an offline puzzle: guess the passphrase, verify locally, repeat.
Why does cracking only work on weak passphrases?

The handshake check is a fast hash, so GPUs test millions of candidates — but only from the wordlist. A 20-character random passphrase is not in any list, so the attack exhausts itself. Length beats everything.

A deauth frame tells a connected device it was disconnected, forcing a reconnect — and a fresh handshake to capture. It works because management frames are unauthenticated on WPA2. Send them only to your own devices in your own lab.
How do I make my WiFi uncrackable?

Use WPA3 (or WPA2-AES minimum), a 20+ character random passphrase, turn WPS off, keep a separate guest network, and update router firmware. Then audit yourself with this guide and watch the crack fail.
flags: Enable/stop monitor mode on the adapter.
Deauth your own client to force a handshake.
Crack the .cap file with a wordlist.
Lock a channel to stop hopping.
how: Put your adapter in monitor mode.
Survey networks and lock onto YOUR router.
Capture the handshake (reconnect your own phone).
Crack the .cap with rockyou on your own network.
Harden: WPA3, long passphrase, WPS off, guest net.
install_cmd:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install aircrack-ng
install_note: On Kali Linux the full Aircrack-ng suite is pre-installed. Debian/Ubuntu users install the aircrack-ng package; you still need a monitor-mode-capable adapter.
issues: The driver does not support it or NetworkManager fights airmon-ng. Kill interfering processes with airmon-ng check kill, use a known-good USB adapter, and retry.
No device connected/reconnected during capture, or you hopped channels. Lock -c to your channel, connect your own phone to force the 4-way exchange, and wait.
Your passphrase is strong — that is success, not failure. Verify with a known-weak lab passphrase first to confirm the workflow, then celebrate the strong one.
Normal on some drivers: the interface renames to wlan0mon. Run iwconfig to find the new name and use it in airodump-ng.
name: Aircrack-ng
overview_p1: Aircrack-ng audits WiFi the way attackers do: listen in monitor mode, capture your router's 4-way handshake, and test it against a wordlist — all offline, all on your own network.
overview_p2: Weak passphrases fall in minutes; 20-character random ones never fall at all. Run this guide against your own router, then set the passphrase that survives it.
reqs: Your own router (admin access to verify)
Your own phone/laptop to force reconnects
Written permission if the network is not yours
schema_desc: Step-by-step Aircrack-ng reference: monitor mode, handshake capture and wordlist audit of your own WiFi, plus hardening.

steps.box: wlan0mon is your new interface. Confirm with iwconfig: Mode:Monitor means every nearby frame now reaches your tools.
steps.code:
sudo airmon-ng check kill
sudo airmon-ng start wlan0
# monitor mode enabled on wlan0mon
steps.desc: Kill blockers, enable monitor mode on your adapter:
steps.title: Step 1 — Monitor Mode

steps.box: Find YOUR router's BSSID and channel in the list. Lock on with --bssid and -c so hopping never loses the handshake.
steps.code:
sudo airodump-ng wlan0mon
# YOUR BSSID, channel 6, WPA2
steps.desc: Survey nearby networks, identify your own router:
steps.title: Step 2 — Survey

steps.box: TOP RIGHT shows WPA handshake when captured — that is your cue. The .cap file now holds an offline puzzle solvable only by guessing.
steps.code:
sudo airodump-ng -c 6 --bssid AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF -w home wlan0mon
# reconnect YOUR phone -> WPA handshake
steps.desc: Capture your router's handshake as your own device reconnects:
steps.title: Step 3 — Capture Handshake

steps.box: Offline means unlimited tries with zero noise. Weak lab passphrases fall here; strong ones exhaust every list — proving the defense works.
steps.code:
aircrack-ng -w rockyou.txt home-01.cap
# KEY FOUND! [ labpass123 ]
steps.desc: Test the capture against a wordlist (your network only):
steps.title: Step 4 — Crack (Your Network)
